findings.element: .b-plan / keepInBand() in render-b.js:821-848 — owner-editing at every desk width (1152, 1279, 1280, 1440)
findings.problem: The lock promises that the date control 'moves the item on the measure while you hold it, and moves nothing else'. At desk it moves everything else. Driven at 1440x960 from a cold owner-editing: the edited row's copy sits 445px into a 664px pane, free = 648; one press of 'Move a week later' puts it at 571 and its bottom at 650 — TWO pixels past the band. keepInBand does not correct by two pixels, it re-centres: pane.scrollTop 0 -> 287 in a single frame (sampled every rAF for 25 frames: 0,287,287,...), while the row itself glides 126px over 0.22s. Net on screen, the moment you told to go a week LATER travels 161px UP, and the six other moments and the whole horizon column slide up 287px under it — the one animated thing in the product destroyed by an instant snap beneath it. What leaves the pane on that first press is the fixed point the entire direction is built on: 'DAYS AWAY' and the 'Today, 16 July' origin mark are on screen before the press and gone after it, and eight consecutive presses never bring them back (origin off the pane 8/8 at 1152, 1279, 1280 and 1440). The jump recurs on roughly every other press and is never small: 287/384/372 at 1440, 317/258/378/252 at 1280, 258/252/252/252 at 1279 and 1152. This is the owner's most repeated action on the surface where they will spend hours, and it is unguarded: interaction-check.mjs runs its in-band loop only at 390 and 768 (lines 1092-1103), where the sheet is fixed and this branch never executes. At 390 the same press moves the row 98px down and scrolls nothing, which is what the desk should feel like. The felt result is not 'my plan moved', it is 'the app took the page away from me'.

biggestWin: The 79. A numeral at 148/96 with its mono 'days' tucked under the descender is the first thing the audience sees, and the composition then spends the rest of the plan earning it back: the same figure returns as the count beside the terminus at the foot of the measure 1,692px later, again on the chat card as '79 days away when this was sent', and again on the printed sheet as '79 days away on Thursday 16 July 2026'. One number, stated four times in four media, never restated as a different grammar. It is the reason the received screen reads as a keepsake rather than a schedule, and it survives the ground flip intact — the ink room is the same room at night, not a filter over the paper one, right down to the chat plate staying somebody else's white surface in both. The morning screen replacing that numeral with the word 'Today' at the same size, over 'This is the day the plan was for.', is the payoff, and it lands.
